requirements.description: Onboarding foundation (ONBD-01..04): first-launch only via DataStore flag, routing before NavHost renders, skippable at any step, v0.1 upgraders with permissions auto-skip
requirements.why: First impression for user testing without trapping existing users

requirements.description: Permission walkthrough (PERM-01..05): priming screen per permission, opens correct Settings screen (NLS, Usage Access, DND), detects grant on return with checkmark, step progress, degraded mode with messaging when skipped
requirements.why: App is useless without special permissions; users need context before Settings

requirements.description: Welcome & tour (TOUR-01..04): welcome screen, 5-tab HorizontalPager tour with dots, quick setup offering Night Mode preset, tour revisitable from Settings
requirements.why: Communicates value and gets one rule active immediately

requirements.description: Habit learning suggestions: heuristic rule suggestions (e.g. >90% dismiss over 7 days, time-window dismissals) shown as accept/modify/dismiss cards
Screen time soft and hard blocking: full-screen overlay with "Continue anyway" (soft) or no bypass for configured duration (hard), plus schedule blocks and cooldowns
Context conditions and lock/sound profiles: location (geofence/WiFi), calendar, charging, Bluetooth conditions; volume/ringer/DND/lock-timeout actions; named presets (Home, Work, Sleep, Meeting)
Stats dashboards and retention: notification volume/heatmap/trends, usage charts vs previous periods, configurable retention (default 30d) with WorkManager cleanup
requirements.why: Awareness half of the core value

requirements.description: Contextual guidance and enhanced permission UX (GUID-01/02, PERM-06/07): coach marks per tab, tooltips on key UI, NLS requestRebind after grant, per-tab degraded-feature explanations
No mandatory permission gate, account creation, long marketing carousel, mascot, personalization quiz, or push-notification opt-in
requirements.why: Each adds friction or breaks trust for an offline utility app

artifacts.full_content:
# AndroidUsageControl

## Vision
A personal, privacy-first Android app (everything local, no internet/auth) that acts as an intelligent assistant for managing notifications, screen time, lock state, and sound via user-defined rules and learned habits. Personal use first; quality bar high enough for later public release.

**Core value:** Help users become aware of and take control of their phone usage patterns without sacrificing privacy.

## Five Pillars
1. **Notification History** — NotificationListenerService capture → Room; browse/filter/search; stats; configurable retention (default 30d) via WorkManager.
2. **Dismissal Rules** — conditions (app, keyword, time, day, priority/category, sender) → dismiss / mute / snooze; every firing logged.
3. **Habit Learning** — heuristics first (dismiss-vs-open ratio, time-to-dismiss, >90% dismiss over 7d → suggest rule); ML-ready data model (TFLite later); card-based suggestions.
4. **Screen Time** — UsageStatsManager; dashboards; daily limits, schedule blocks, cooldowns; enforcement advisory / soft block / hard block via SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW overlay + foreground service.
5. **Lock & Sound** — conditions (WiFi/geofence, time, calendar, charging, Bluetooth) → volume, ringer, DND, lock timeout; named presets (Home, Work, Sleep, Meeting).

## Unified Rules Engine
Shared composable conditions; per-pillar actions. `Rule { id, name, enabled, priority, conditions (AND), conditionGroups (OR between, AND within), actions, pillar: NOTIFICATION|SCREEN_TIME|LOCK_SOUND, createdBy: USER|SUGGESTION|LEARNED }`.

## Stack
Kotlin, Jetpack Compose + Material 3, MVVM/clean architecture, Hilt, Room, Coroutines/Flow, WorkManager + foreground service, Gradle version catalogs. minSdk 29.

## Modules
`app/`; `core/{core-common, core-database, core-rules, core-ui, core-model}`; `feature/{feature-notifications, feature-learning, feature-screentime, feature-lockcontrol, feature-settings, feature-onboarding, feature-rules}`; `service/{service-notification, service-usage, service-context}`.

## Milestone Sequence
- [x] M001: v0.1 Scaffold — Module structure and basic stubs only; pillars not yet functional end-to-end
- [x] M002: v0.2 User Testing — Onboarding, permission walkthrough, welcome tour and quick setup (device-verified, Maestro E2E)
- [ ] M003: v0.3 Learning & Blocking — Habit learning suggestions, screen time soft/hard blocking
- [ ] M004: v0.4 Context & Lock — Location/calendar context, lock control, sound profiles
- [ ] M005: v0.5 Polish — Stats dashboards, configurable retention, settings polish
- [ ] M006: v1.0 Stable Release — Stable personal release, all pillars fully functional

Later (v1.x+): ML learning, widgets, backup/export, public release polish.

## Sources ingested
PROJECT.md, README.md, .planning/{REQUIREMENTS,ROADMAP,STATE}.md, .planning/phases/*/SUMMARY.md. `.planning/codebase/*` left in place as architecture reference.

# M007: v0.3 Doorman

**Vision:** The app becomes Doorman: new name, LED-motif dark-first theme on Material 3 Expressive, three tabs (Now, Apps, Modes), and a listener that captures everything later lanes and mirroring need. The Now stream is the daily surface. Phone behaviour is unchanged; nothing is mirrored or held yet.

## Success Criteria

- Doorman name, theme and three tabs live on device
- Listener data model complete enough for v0.4 mirroring

## Slices

- [ ] **S01: Toolchain and theme** `risk:high` `depends:[]`
  > After this: Launcher shows Doorman with LED-dot icon; preview gallery renders every shared component in dark and light

- [ ] **S02: Listener foundation** `risk:high` `depends:[]`
  > After this: Post/update/remove a test notification yields one row with correct reason and update count; icons load after listener restart

- [ ] **S03: Shell and Now** `risk:medium` `depends:[S01,S02]`
  > After this: Bottom bar Now/Apps/Modes; Now shows real notifications with icons and lane dots, swipe archive with undo, swipe-left snooze to time, tap opens original

- [ ] **S04: Apps and Modes v1** `risk:medium` `depends:[S03]`
  > After this: Apps lists apps by alerts/day with sparklines; app profile shows stats, channels, limit, suggestions; Modes shows preset cards whose toggle applies the sound profile

## Boundary Map

Not provided.
<!-- gsd:state-version=25:1 -->

# M008: v0.4 Lanes

**Vision:** Lanes are the product: user-defined buckets with colour, delivery policy, decay and breakthroughs. New senders are screened once and routed forever, non-Instant lanes are mirrored under Doorman's channels, batches deliver at set times or breakpoints, and everything removed is restorable from a searchable archive.

## Slices

- [ ] **S01: Lanes and Screener** `[sketch]` `risk:medium` `depends:[]`
  > After this: New sender triggers Screener; one tap routes it and re-files its history

- [ ] **S02: Mirroring and policies** `[sketch]` `risk:high` `depends:[S01]`
  > After this: A Quiet-lane notification appears as a Doorman mirror with lane colour, original icon and working open/reply

- [ ] **S03: Batching and delivery** `[sketch]` `risk:high` `depends:[S02]`
  > After this: Batched lane holds notifications and delivers a summary at 12:30 with Open / Deliver all / Keep holding

- [ ] **S04: Archive and memory** `[sketch]` `risk:low` `depends:[S02]`
  > After this: Search the archive, restore a batch, open a keyword page, read the daily digest

## Boundary Map

# M009: v0.5 Modes and bridge

**Vision:** Presets become modes that change lanes and block apps; screen-time enforcement becomes friction instead of walls; an opt-in SemPKM bridge sends context (never content) and receives persona switches.

## Slices

- [ ] **S01: Modes** `[sketch]` `risk:medium` `depends:[]`
  > After this: Deep Work mode makes Work lane instant and releases held batches at exit

- [ ] **S02: Screen-time friction** `[sketch]` `risk:low` `depends:[S01]`

- [ ] **S03: SemPKM bridge** `[sketch]` `risk:high` `depends:[S01]`

decisions.choice: One unified rules engine (core-rules) with shared composable conditions (AND within groups, OR between groups) and per-pillar actions
decisions.rationale: Avoids three divergent rule systems; lets learned suggestions emit the same Rule type

decisions.choice: Privacy-first, fully local: Room storage, no accounts, no internet, no push notifications
decisions.rationale: Core value is control without sacrificing privacy; auth/push add friction and destroy trust

decisions.choice: Kotlin, Compose + Material 3, MVVM/clean layers, Hilt, Room, Coroutines/Flow, WorkManager + foreground service, Gradle version catalogs; multi-module app/core-*/feature-*/service-*; minSdk 29
decisions.rationale: Modern Android standard; module boundaries keep pillars independent and iterable

decisions.choice: Heuristics first (dismiss ratio, time-to-dismiss thresholds); store interaction vectors from day one so a TFLite model can be added later
decisions.rationale: Ship useful suggestions early while keeping ML path open

decisions.choice: Per-rule level: advisory notification, soft block overlay with bypass, hard block overlay without bypass; via SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW + foreground service polling
decisions.rationale: Lets user pick friction level per rule

decisions.choice: Splash routing: startDestination null (empty Box) until DataStore onboarding_complete resolves; nested onboarding/main graphs with popUpTo(onboarding){inclusive=true}
decisions.rationale: Prevents back-navigation into onboarding and NavHost flicker; high recovery cost if wrong

decisions.decision: Onboarding state persistence and upgrader handling
decisions.choice: Single @Singleton DataStore from app DataStoreModule; onboarding_complete written only by PermissionWalkthroughViewModel; v0.1 users with all permissions granted get the flag written on first launch
decisions.rationale: Multiple DataStore instances corrupt; single writer avoids double-writes; upgraders skip onboarding

decisions.choice: PermissionChecker in core-common shared by onboarding and settings; special permissions never via checkSelfPermission (usage access via AppOpsManager.unsafeCheckOpNoThrow); NLS ComponentName passed as string to avoid feature→service deps
decisions.rationale: Special permissions aren't reported by checkSelfPermission; keeps module graph clean

decisions.choice: Degraded mode, never a mandatory gate; non-dismissable DegradedPermissionBanner(message: String) persists while permission missing, feature text owned by feature modules
decisions.rationale: Mandatory gates force abandonment; hiding the banner hides a real problem
